verifiedSound.reasoning: Each displacement resets deadline to min(now+P, H). The heir can always re-initiate at H, and from H onward abortClaim is closed, so the total delay a runaway owner key can cause without extendHorizon is at most H + W.

verifiedSound.property: Boundary comparisons are consistent, with no gaps or overlaps
verifiedSound.reasoning: 'Horizon reached' is `>= absoluteDeadline` everywhere (314, 464, 492, 509, 540, 670, views 804/825); a partial withdraw clears only at `< absoluteDeadline` (574). initiateClaim is allowed at `>= deadline`, matching warningsOf bit 0 and getVault.expired. finalizeClaim is allowed at `>= finalizableAt`, matching getVault.finalizable (829). The createVault and extendHorizon floors and ceilings use the same inclusive bounds.

verifiedSound.property: A hostile heir or third party cannot bring the claim date forward
verifiedSound.reasoning: Only owner-keyed functions and checkInByChain write `deadline`, and they only reset it to now+P (never lower for a given P; P changes only by owner action, which itself resets the clock). topUp never touches the clock. challengeWindow has no setter. claimInitiatedAt is always block.timestamp.

verifiedSound.property: No third party can shorten the deadline with the hash chain
verifiedSound.reasoning: checkInByChain calls _resetClock, which gives min(now+P, H). Under the same P that is at least the previous deadline, and preimages are one-way, so a captured preimage can only be replayed as the same liveness extension (541-545).

verifiedSound.property: Neither the heir nor a third party can block the owner's veto inside the window
verifiedSound.reasoning: abortClaim makes no external calls and depends only on owner-controlled state. While CLAIM_PENDING, the only third-party mutator that applies is finalizeClaim, which is gated to after the window (topUp, checkInByChain and initiateClaim all require ACTIVE). PoC P4: even when the window straddles the horizon, extendHorizon still vetoes for the whole window.

verifiedSound.property: finalizeClaim is permissionless and no heir, recipient, token, admin or third party can block it
verifiedSound.reasoning: It makes no external calls (settlement goes to the credit lane). totalLocked >= balance holds on every path, so 702 cannot underflow. The fee is at most 1% and is zero when feeRecipient is unset. _removeFromOpen keeps openIndex consistent (333), and each vault is removed at most once because the terminal states are absorbing.

verifiedSound.property: SETTLED and CLOSED are terminal
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every mutator checks state: _requireLive (282-285) for withdraw/setBeneficiary/setInactivityPeriod/extendHorizon/setCheckInChain; ACTIVE-only checks for checkIn/checkInMany/checkInByChain/topUp/initiateClaim; CLAIM_PENDING-only checks for abortClaim/finalizeClaim.

verifiedSound.property: Owner and beneficiary cannot be the same address
verifiedSound.reasoning: createVault (381) and setBeneficiary (584) reject beneficiary == msg.sender, and the vault owner is fixed as msg.sender at creation with no transfer function (PoC P10). A payout recipient equal to the owner is allowed and harmless.

verifiedSound.property: Changing the beneficiary while a claim is pending behaves correctly
verifiedSound.reasoning: Before the horizon it clears the claim and resets the clock, so the new heir waits a full period. Past the horizon it reverts HorizonReached, which protects the running claim. claimRecipient is fixed at initiation and no one can re-point it.

verifiedSound.property: A late check-in race cannot deny the owner before the horizon
verifiedSound.reasoning: PoC P9: at t == deadline the heir can win the race with initiateClaim; the owner's checkIn reverts ClaimPendingUseAbort, but abortClaim still works and resets the clock.

verifiedSound.property: The admin cannot affect the state machine
verifiedSound.reasoning: Admin functions (742-780) write only claimFeeBps, feeRecipient, creationPaused and surplus. None touches vault state, deadlines, beneficiaries or claims; the pause gates only createVault.

verifiedSound.property: Reentrancy cannot corrupt state transitions
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every state-changing entry point is nonReentrant. topUp re-checks ACTIVE after _pull (450). initiateClaim, abortClaim and finalizeClaim make no external calls.

verifiedSound.property: The fee locked at initiation does not survive a cancelled claim
verifiedSound.reasoning: lockedFeeBps is overwritten at every initiateClaim (652) and read only in finalizeClaim, which requires CLAIM_PENDING (B-05 fix verified).

verifiedSound.property: OQ-1 (chain check-in sniping) is disclosed accurately
verifiedSound.reasoning: checkInByChain requires ACTIVE (537), so once the heir initiates, the seed cannot veto. Only the owner key (abortClaim or soft actions before the horizon, extendHorizon or a full withdraw after) can, which matches the NatSpec at 529-533.

verifiedSound.property: The list of admin functions is complete
verifiedSound.reasoning: The only onlyOwner functions are setClaimFee, setFeeRecipient, setCreationPaused and sweepSurplus, plus the inherited transferOwnership; acceptOwnership needs the pending owner. None of them writes _vaults. None writes _credits either: the only write that benefits the admin is the fee credit inside the permissionless finalizeClaim.

verifiedSound.property: The admin cannot change a beneficiary or any vault parameter
verifiedSound.reasoning: v.beneficiary, inactivityPeriod, absoluteDeadline, challengeWindow, feeBps and state are written only in owner-gated functions (msg.sender == vault owner through _vault(msg.sender, id)), in the beneficiary-gated initiateClaim, or in the permissionless finalizeClaim. No admin path reaches them.

verifiedSound.property: The admin cannot cancel, redirect or block an owner withdrawal
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdraw (:552-580) reads no admin state and credits `to` in the same transaction. withdrawCredit and pushCredit (:714-733) read no admin state, and no admin function touches _credits.

verifiedSound.property: The admin cannot block a valid claim settlement
verifiedSound.reasoning: finalizeClaim (:682-710) makes no external call. It reads claimFeeBps and feeRecipient only as values, and fee <= amt, so nothing can underflow. PoC P5: a reverting-contract recipient, and a recipient equal to the heir, both settle normally.

verifiedSound.property: The creation pause does not block existing vaults
verifiedSound.reasoning: Only createVault checks creationPaused (:378). topUp, checkIn, checkInMany, checkInByChain, the owner actions, initiateClaim, abortClaim, finalizeClaim, withdrawCredit and pushCredit ignore it (PoC P5).

verifiedSound.property: The fee cannot exceed 1% (hard cap)
verifiedSound.reasoning: The constructor (:269) and setClaimFee (:743) both revert above MAX_CLAIM_FEE_BPS = 100, and no other code writes claimFeeBps. The live value is 50.

verifiedSound.property: Each vault's fee ceiling cannot be changed after creation
verifiedSound.reasoning: v.feeBps is written only in createVault (:411). lockedFeeBps = min(global, feeBps) (:652), and the settlement rate = min(lockedFeeBps, global) (:695-697), so it is always <= the creation ceiling.

verifiedSound.property: Once a claim starts, the fee rate can only fall
verifiedSound.reasoning: finalizeClaim takes min(lockedFeeBps, current claimFeeBps). Raising the global rate after initiation has no effect, and cutting it reaches the heir (existing A-04 tests). The fee-recipient dimension is the exception: see the recipient-toggle finding.

verifiedSound.property: A stale locked rate cannot leak into a later claim
verifiedSound.reasoning: STATE_CLAIM_PENDING can only be entered through initiateClaim, which always rewrites lockedFeeBps, so a value left from an aborted or superseded claim is overwritten before any finalize.

verifiedSound.property: With no fee recipient at settlement, no fee is taken
verifiedSound.reasoning: At :699, fee = 0 when feeTo == address(0), and nothing is credited to the zero address. This holds at the moment of settlement; the recipient-toggle finding covers the lock gap.

verifiedSound.property: Fee arithmetic and base are correct
verifiedSound.reasoning: fee = amt * bps / 10000 with floor rounding, so it never exceeds bps. amt <= 2^128 and bps <= 100, so the product cannot overflow. The base is the whole accounted v.balance at settlement. Deposits, top-ups, check-ins, owner withdrawals and credit withdrawals are never charged.

verifiedSound.property: Accounting is conserved at settlement
verifiedSound.reasoning: totalLocked[token] -= amt and totalCredited[token] += (amt - fee) + fee. Credits go into the mapping only, so a recipient that reverts, is blocklisted, or is the heir itself cannot jam settlement.

verifiedSound.property: Changing the fee recipient between initiation and settlement only changes who gets the fee
verifiedSound.reasoning: feeTo is read at finalize and gets the fee credit. The amount depends only on bps (and on the recipient being nonzero). The heir's credit and past recipients' credits are untouched.

verifiedSound.property: The contract cannot pay fees to itself
verifiedSound.reasoning: The constructor (:270) and setFeeRecipient (:751) reject address(this), and _payout (:359) rejects paying itself, so fee revenue cannot be stranded in the credited lane that way.

verifiedSound.property: Constructor validation
verifiedSound.reasoning: A fee above the cap reverts (FeeTooHigh). initialAdmin == 0 reverts through OZ Ownable (OwnableInvalidOwner). A zero recipient is allowed and means no fee. The deployed parameters match deployments/base.json (50 bps).

verifiedSound.property: Two-step ownership handover
verifiedSound.reasoning: OZ 5.6.1 Ownable2Step: transferOwnership only sets pendingOwner, and only that address can acceptOwnership. Live read at Base block 51710768: owner 0x883C…CdCA3, pendingOwner 0 on both contracts.

verifiedSound.property: renounceOwnership is disabled, and users do not depend on the admin being active
verifiedSound.reasoning: On both contracts it is a pure override that always reverts. No user flow (withdraw, claim, finalize, credits) reads the admin, so a lost admin key only freezes admin revenue, sweeps and pause changes.

verifiedSound.property: sweepSurplus cannot touch native coin or ordinary single-entry ERC20s
verifiedSound.reasoning: surplus = balance - (locked + credited), floored at 0. Native coin cannot arrive outside createVault/topUp because receive() reverts and there is no fallback, except by force-feeding, which lands in surplus. The sweep is nonReentrant and rejects a zero or self target. Live surplus(native) = 0.

verifiedSound.property: The native-coin marker cannot collide with a token
verifiedSound.reasoning: token == address(0) always takes the native path. The ERC20 path requires msg.value == 0 and a contract with code (a no-code address reverts in balanceOf decoding and in SafeERC20). token == address(this) reverts, so native and ERC20 accounting cannot mix.

verifiedSound.property: NotifySubscription admin limits
verifiedSound.reasoning: setPrice enforces a price > 0. Time already bought (paidUntil) cannot be revoked. minSecondsAdded protects payers against a setPrice front-run. withdraw moves only subscription revenue, by design, and renounce is disabled.

verifiedSound.property: Inbound fee-on-transfer tokens are recorded at the amount actually received
verifiedSound.reasoning: _pull (:345-356) records balanceOf(this) after the transfer minus before, and createVault/topUp write that figure to v.balance, totalLocked and the VaultCreated/ToppedUp events. If a token shrinks the vault's balance during the transfer, the subtraction underflows and the call reverts. Nothing is ever mis-recorded.

verifiedSound.property: Tokens that return no bool work; tokens that return false are refused
verifiedSound.reasoning: OZ 5.6.1 SafeERC20 accepts empty return data only when the target has code, and treats any return value other than 1 as a failure. The PoC ran a USDT-ABI token through the full lifecycle, and a returns-false token reverted with SafeERC20FailedOperation.

verifiedSound.property: Tokens that revert on zero-value transfers are safe
verifiedSound.reasoning: No code path issues a zero-value transfer. amount==0 reverts in createVault, topUp and withdraw; credit pulls revert with NothingCredited; sweeps revert with NoSurplus; a zero fee is never credited (:704); and the heir's share amt-fee is at least 1 because the fee is at most 1% and amt is at least 1.

verifiedSound.property: A token address with no code, a precompile address, or the vault's own address is rejected
verifiedSound.reasoning: The balanceOf STATICCALL gets empty or undecodable return data and the call reverts before any state is written. The vault has no fallback, so token == address(this) also reverts. The PoC checked an EOA, precompiles 1-10 and the vault address.

verifiedSound.property: Native value sent with an ERC20 operation is refused
verifiedSound.reasoning: _pull reverts with UnexpectedNativeValue when msg.value != 0 for any non-native token. It is the only ERC20 entry point for both payable functions (createVault, topUp); every other function is non-payable, and receive() reverts.

verifiedSound.property: ERC777/ERC1363-style hooks cannot re-enter the vault
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every state-changing user function is nonReentrant: createVault, topUp, checkIn, checkInMany, setCheckInChain, checkInByChain, withdraw, setBeneficiary, setInactivityPeriod, extendHorizon, initiateClaim, abortClaim, finalizeClaim, withdrawCredit, pushCredit and sweepSurplus. The only unguarded functions are onlyOwner setters and views. The PoC showed a hook re-entering topUp or withdrawCredit reverts with ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall. The post-transfer re-check in topUp (:450) is now redundant but harmless.

verifiedSound.property: The deposit measurement cannot be used to draw on other users' funds or approvals
verifiedSound.reasoning: _pull always pulls from msg.sender, and the vault never approves or pulls from anyone else. A donation during the measurement only increases the depositor's own vault. The PoC confirmed other lanes and surplus stay unchanged.

verifiedSound.property: Users' standing approvals to the vault cannot be spent by anyone else
verifiedSound.reasoning: The only transferFrom in the contract is safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, amount) at :352. There is no arbitrary-`from` path, so max approvals granted by the app or tests are safe.

verifiedSound.property: A hostile token cannot contaminate other tokens' lanes or the native lane
verifiedSound.reasoning: totalLocked, totalCredited and _credits are all keyed by token address, and no function moves value between keys. A lying token can distort only its own lane (the one exception is the double-entry finding, where two addresses share a ledger). ERC20 paths never send native value.

verifiedSound.property: Pausable and blocklisting tokens cannot stall the inheritance state machine
verifiedSound.reasoning: checkIn, abortClaim, withdraw, initiateClaim and finalizeClaim make no token calls, so pause or blocklist can only delay credit pulls. The PoC showed a vault settles and checkIn works while the token is blocked or paused.

verifiedSound.property: A blocklisted owner, heir or fee recipient can still be paid under two-sided blocklists (USDC style)
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdrawCredit(token, to) lets the credited account choose `to`, and the token sees only the vault as sender. The PoC routed a blocklisted owner's credit to a clean address. A pushCredit to a two-sided-blocklisted account reverts rather than stranding the funds.

verifiedSound.property: A failed payout never corrupts the credit lane
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdrawCredit and pushCredit zero the credit and reduce totalCredited before the transfer, inside nonReentrant, and any revert in the transfer (hook, blocklist, pause, cap) rolls the whole call back, credit included.

verifiedSound.property: Oversized balances revert instead of truncating
verifiedSound.reasoning: createVault and topUp convert with SafeCast.toUint128, and withdraw checks amount <= v.balance before the uint128 downcast at :561. Tokens with supplies above 2^128 fail cleanly.

verifiedSound.property: For standard single-address tokens, the lanes stay solvent and the admin can sweep only force-fed value
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every change to v.balance is matched by a change to totalLocked (:421, :452, :562, :702), and every credit change is matched in totalCredited (:340, :719, :730). For tokens whose balance moves only through the vault's own transfers, balance >= locked + credited, so surplus() is exactly the unaccounted excess.

verifiedSound.property: No fee is charged on deposits or owner withdrawals in any token
verifiedSound.reasoning: The fee is computed only in finalizeClaim (:695-704), capped by lockedFeeBps, the current rate and the MAX_CLAIM_FEE_BPS constant (100). It is zero when feeRecipient is unset.

verifiedSound.property: NotifySubscription has no ERC20 attack surface
verifiedSound.reasoning: It never calls a token and holds only native coin. The one side effect is that ERC20 sent to it by mistake cannot be recovered, since there is no sweep; this has no user-fund impact because the contract is retired.

verifiedSound.property: A chain check-in can never move the deadline past the absolute horizon
verifiedSound.reasoning: _resetClock (:287-291) clamps deadline to absoluteDeadline, and both checkInByChain (:540) and setCheckInChain (:509) revert at or after the horizon; the PoC confirms the deadline equals the horizon and HorizonReached fires after it.

verifiedSound.property: The chain is liveness only, never authority
verifiedSound.reasoning: checkInByChain requires STATE_ACTIVE (:537), so it cannot touch a pending, settled or closed vault, and no chain path reaches withdraw, setBeneficiary, abortClaim or extendHorizon; the PoC confirms VaultNotActive on pending and settled vaults.

verifiedSound.property: Only the vault owner can install or replace a chain
verifiedSound.reasoning: setCheckInChain resolves storage via _vault(msg.sender, vaultId) (:504), so a caller can only reach their own vaults, and _requireLive rejects terminal vaults.

verifiedSound.property: Zero or out-of-range chain parameters are rejected
verifiedSound.reasoning: anchor 0, count 0 and count > 100,000 revert InvalidCheckInChain (:503); an uninstalled chain reverts InvalidCheckInChain (:538); an exhausted counter reverts CheckInChainExhausted (:539).

verifiedSound.property: No off-by-one or underflow in the contract's counter/anchor update
verifiedSound.reasoning: Each call verifies exactly one hash step, replaces the anchor with the verified preimage and decrements hbLeft only after the hbLeft == 0 check (checked arithmetic), so anchor H^n with count n gives exactly n uses.

verifiedSound.property: No replay within a single vault/installation
verifiedSound.reasoning: After a use the anchor is the spent value, so resubmitting it hits CheckInAlreadyUsed (:541), older values fail the hash check (BadCheckIn), and skipping ahead fails BadCheckIn (repo test and PoC).

verifiedSound.property: Front-running a chain check-in by copying the preimage is harmless
verifiedSound.reasoning: The state change does not depend on msg.sender and the event is keyed by vaultOwner, so a copier produces the same deadline in the same or an adjacent block; the victim's transaction merely reverts.

verifiedSound.property: The heir cannot front-run a chain check-in that lands before the deadline
verifiedSound.reasoning: initiateClaim requires block.timestamp >= deadline (:644), and transactions in the same block share a timestamp, so the race exists only at or after the deadline (see OQ-1 finding).

verifiedSound.property: A chain check-in never shortens the deadline
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every write to deadline or inactivityPeriod goes through _resetClock, so deadline <= lastReset + currentPeriod <= now + period, which is what a check-in sets.

verifiedSound.property: Hash primitive and encoding are sound
verifiedSound.reasoning: abi.encodePacked(bytes32) is exactly 32 bytes with no packing ambiguity, keccak256 gives 2^256 preimage resistance, and iterated-hash image shrinkage over 100,000 steps is negligible (about 2^240 remaining); the only defect is missing domain separation.

verifiedSound.property: Gas and DoS are bounded regardless of chain length
verifiedSound.reasoning: Verification is one keccak with no loop; measured at 50,475 gas per check-in on a 100,000-step chain, and generation is off-chain.

verifiedSound.property: A third party without a valid preimage cannot alter or exhaust someone's chain
verifiedSound.reasoning: hbAnchor and hbLeft are written only by owner-gated setCheckInChain and by checkInByChain after a successful hash check, and checkInByChain is nonReentrant with no external calls.

verifiedSound.property: setCheckInChain displacing a pending claim is owner-authenticated and closed at the horizon
verifiedSound.reasoning: It is owner-gated, reverts at or after absoluteDeadline (:509), and _clearPending (:314) independently refuses displacement past the horizon, so it cannot become an unbounded veto loop.

verifiedSound.property: The prior A-01 reentrancy fix covers every state-changing function
verifiedSound.reasoning: All 15 non-admin state-changing functions plus sweepSurplus carry nonReentrant. The unguarded ones (setClaimFee, setFeeRecipient, setCreationPaused, transferOwnership, acceptOwnership, renounceOwnership) make no external calls and require msg.sender to be the admin or pending admin. A token or recipient callback cannot be the admin's EOA.

verifiedSound.property: The list of external calls is complete and small
verifiedSound.reasoning: There are only three kinds. (1) In _pull (createVault, topUp): token.balanceOf as a read-only call and token.transferFrom(msg.sender, vault, amount). (2) In _payout (withdrawCredit, pushCredit, sweepSurplus): a native send or token.transfer. (3) In surplus(): token.balanceOf. There is no approve, no delegatecall and no call with caller-supplied data.

verifiedSound.property: Payouts update state before transferring and cannot half-complete
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdrawCredit and pushCredit zero the credit and reduce totalCredited before _payout. A failed native send reverts with NativeTransferFailed and a failed token transfer reverts through SafeERC20, so a failure undoes everything. Tested: pushes to gas-guzzling and reverting contracts reverted and the credit was unchanged.

verifiedSound.property: Deposit measurement cannot be double-counted or written onto a closed vault
verifiedSound.reasoning: createVault and topUp are the only places that call a token before writing state. The single contract-wide lock stops an ERC777-style hook from starting a second deposit inside the first, so the same balance change cannot be counted twice. The hook also cannot close or claim the vault mid-deposit, and topUp re-checks that the vault is still active after the transfer.

verifiedSound.property: The permissionless topUp cannot spend anyone else's token approval
verifiedSound.reasoning: _pull always takes tokens from msg.sender, and the vault never approves any spender, so there is no approval that could be drained.

verifiedSound.property: A hostile heir or payout address cannot block settlement
verifiedSound.reasoning: finalizeClaim and withdraw make no external call; they only record credits. Tested: finalizeClaim succeeded with a reverting contract, a gas-guzzling contract and a contract returning 200 kB of data as the claim recipient.

verifiedSound.property: The 63/64 gas rule and oversized return data only hurt the caller's own transaction
verifiedSound.reasoning: The native send in _payout copies all returned data (gas rose from 44k to 467k when the recipient returned 300 kB), while SafeERC20 5.6.1 copies at most 32 bytes on success. Either way, the only destination that can trigger this is one the credit holder chose (the `to` in withdrawCredit, or the account itself in pushCredit). Running out of gas makes the whole transaction revert, never a silent partial payout.

verifiedSound.property: One user cannot jam another user's payout
verifiedSound.reasoning: The lock only lasts for one transaction. Credits are stored per token and per account, and no function loops over recipients. In testing, the fee recipient withdrew normally after several hostile heir recipients had failed.

verifiedSound.property: No credit can be recorded for address(0) or for the vault itself
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdraw rejects to==0 and to==this. initiateClaim rejects recipient==0 and recipient==this. A fee is credited only when feeRecipient is non-zero, and both the constructor and setFeeRecipient reject the vault's own address. _payout also rejects the vault's address. Tested.

verifiedSound.property: Credits are paid only to the address the design intends
verifiedSound.reasoning: withdrawCredit pays only the caller's own credit, to the `to` the caller chooses. pushCredit pays the credited account itself. finalizeClaim credits exactly the claimRecipient chosen by the beneficiary (cleared on abort or supersede) and the feeRecipient. No path pays to an address chosen by an unrelated third party.

verifiedSound.property: The two accounting totals always match the individual records
verifiedSound.reasoning: Every _credit call adds the same amount to _credits and totalCredited, and every pull subtracts the same amount from both. createVault and topUp add the same received amount to the vault balance and totalLocked, and withdraw and finalizeClaim subtract it from both. The subtractions therefore cannot underflow for single-address, non-rebasing tokens.

verifiedSound.property: Native coin cannot arrive outside the accounting
verifiedSound.reasoning: receive() reverts and there is no fallback. Only createVault and topUp accept value, and both require msg.value == amount for native vaults and msg.value == 0 for token vaults. Coin forced in by SELFDESTRUCT or block rewards only ever counts as surplus.

verifiedSound.property: A malicious token only affects its own accounting
verifiedSound.reasoning: Totals are kept per token address. A hostile token can inflate only its own totals: re-entering the vault reverts on the lock, and sending native coin reverts in receive(). Native coin and other tokens are untouched.

verifiedSound.property: View functions are consistent while a payout is in flight
verifiedSound.reasoning: During withdrawCredit or pushCredit the state is final before the call, and native value has already left when the recipient's code runs. So creditOf, totalCredited and surplus are correct for native and standard-token payouts. The inconsistency during deposits is reported separately in F4.

verifiedSound.property: NotifySubscription has no reentrancy exposure
verifiedSound.reasoning: subscribe makes no external calls. withdraw is admin-only, sends the whole balance to an admin-chosen address, and writes nothing after the call. There is no receive or fallback, so plain transfers revert.

verifiedSound.property: Every narrowing cast is safe or guarded
verifiedSound.reasoning: uint64(block.timestamp) can only truncate after about 5.8e11 years. uint64(vaultId) comes from a uint64 counter. uint8(ids.length) is < MAX_OPEN_VAULTS (32). Balances go through SafeCast.toUint128 in createVault and topUp, which reverts rather than truncating (PoC P6: topping up a vault at 2^128-1 reverts SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast). withdraw's uint128(amount) runs only after amount <= balance. NotifySubscription's uint64(target) is capped at now + 3650 days.

verifiedSound.property: No time addition can overflow, even with extreme inputs
verifiedSound.reasoning: Inputs are bounded before use: period <= 3650 days, window <= 365 days, absoluteDeadline <= now + 36500 days, all in 0.8.28 checked arithmetic. So now+period, deadline, absoluteDeadline+challengeWindow and claimInitiatedAt+challengeWindow all stay below 2^33. A horizon of type(uint64).max and now+MAX_HORIZON+1 both revert HorizonTooFar (PoC P5). The ABI decoder rejects out-of-range uint32 and uint64 arguments.

verifiedSound.property: Min/max bounds are enforced on every path that writes a timing field
verifiedSound.reasoning: createVault and setInactivityPeriod both check [7 days, 3650 days]. challengeWindow is checked against [7 days, 365 days] and has no setter. extendHorizon requires the new horizon to be > current, >= now + period and <= now + MAX_HORIZON. Its floor is always below its ceiling because MAX_INACTIVITY < MAX_HORIZON.

verifiedSound.property: Extreme but allowed values neither lock funds nor make claims impossible
verifiedSound.reasoning: A full lifecycle at 3650-day period, 365-day window and 100-year horizon, including an extendHorizon to exactly now + MAX_HORIZON, settles correctly (PoC P5). The owner can withdraw at any time, and the longest lost-key delay is bounded by horizon + window.

verifiedSound.property: The deadline never goes past the horizon
verifiedSound.reasoning: deadline is only written by _resetClock, which clamps it to absoluteDeadline. absoluteDeadline only increases (extendHorizon), and every change is followed by _resetClock. So the heir can always initiate at absoluteDeadline.

verifiedSound.property: Horizon guarantee against a lost key or runaway automation
verifiedSound.reasoning: At or after absoluteDeadline, checkIn, checkInMany, checkInByChain, setCheckInChain, abortClaim and every soft action displacing a claim revert. A partial withdraw no longer displaces a claim. The heir can initiate at absoluteDeadline and finalize at absoluteDeadline + challengeWindow (PoC P4). Only extendHorizon (live key, at least one inactivity period of cooldown) or a full withdraw can override it.

verifiedSound.property: All boundary comparisons follow the same rule
verifiedSound.reasoning: Expired or claimable means >= deadline. Horizon reached means >= absoluteDeadline. Finalizable means >= claimInitiatedAt + challengeWindow. The same rule is used in the mutators, warningsOf and getVault. PoC P4 exercises deadline-1 / deadline and finalizableAt-1 / finalizableAt exactly.

verifiedSound.property: Fee arithmetic
verifiedSound.reasoning: The rate is capped at 100 bps in the constructor and setClaimFee; feeBps <= 100 and lockedFeeBps <= feeBps. amt < 2^128, so amt*bps cannot overflow. fee < amt, so amt - fee cannot underflow. Integer division rounds in the heir's favour, and the fee is 0 whenever amt*bps < 10000 (a 99-unit vault at 1% pays 0: PoC P6). There is no splitting route to game the rounding.

verifiedSound.property: No zero-value vaults
verifiedSound.reasoning: amount == 0 reverts ZeroAmount. received == 0 (for example a 100% fee-on-transfer token) reverts NothingReceived. A balance that reaches 0 through withdraw closes the vault atomically. initiateClaim rejects a zero balance. So no ACTIVE or CLAIM_PENDING vault can have a zero balance.

verifiedSound.property: Struct packing and storage layout
verifiedSound.reasoning: The compiled storageLayout matches the declared 6-slot Vault packing with no overlap (owner/createdAt/state/openIndex/feeBps | beneficiary/deadline/inactivityPeriod | token/absoluteDeadline/challengeWindow | balance/claimInitiatedAt/hbLeft | claimRecipient/lockedFeeBps | hbAnchor). OZ 5.6.1 ReentrancyGuard keeps its flag in an ERC-7201 namespaced slot, so it cannot collide with contract storage.

verifiedSound.property: Vault ids are never reused, and stale fields cannot be read back
verifiedSound.reasoning: vaultCount only increases, only in createVault, and no vault is ever deleted. _vault rejects id >= vaultCount. SETTLED and CLOSED are final states: every function that changes a vault first requires ACTIVE, CLAIM_PENDING or _requireLive. So stale openIndex, hbAnchor, hbLeft and lockedFeeBps on a finished vault are never used, and _removeFromOpen runs exactly once per vault.

verifiedSound.property: Invalid heir and payout input never reaches a signature
verifiedSound.reasoning: In actHeir (:229-230) and actClaim (:247-248), ethers.getAddress runs inside the send() closure passed to runTx, so a throw is caught at :112-115 and shown as 'failed'. No wallet prompt opens. In the create form, getAddress at :362/:365 sits inside the try at :360, so a bad address fails before ensureAllowance or createVault. Tested with ethers 6.17.0: mixed-case input with a bad checksum throws 'bad address checksum'.

verifiedSound.lens: r2-frontend: irreversible address inputs and truncated display (AUDIT_SCOPE priority 7, no lens assigned)
verifiedSound.property: A third party cannot change the heir or claim as a lookalike without the owner signing it
verifiedSound.reasoning: setBeneficiary works only on _vault(msg.sender, ...) (:586). initiateClaim requires msg.sender == v.beneficiary as an exact 160-bit comparison (:643). A lookalike gets authority only if the owner names it. Poisoning needs an owner mistake; it cannot be forced on-chain.

verifiedSound.lens: r2-frontend: irreversible address inputs and truncated display (AUDIT_SCOPE priority 7, no lens assigned)
verifiedSound.property: The heir tab compares full addresses, not truncated ones
verifiedSound.reasoning: app.js:387-389 filters on vault.beneficiary.toLowerCase() === S.account.toLowerCase(), a full-address comparison. A real heir who looks up the owner therefore correctly sees that a poisoned vault does not name them. The detection path works, but nothing in the app tells the owner to have the heir use it.

verifiedSound.lens: r2-frontend: irreversible address inputs and truncated display (AUDIT_SCOPE priority 7, no lens assigned)
verifiedSound.property: Owner withdrawals and credit pulls cannot be redirected by pasted addresses
verifiedSound.reasoning: actWithdraw passes S.account as `to` (:223), and the Payouts tab calls withdrawCredit(token, S.account) (:415). Neither owner-side value-exit path takes a free-text destination, so address poisoning cannot redirect them. The only free-text destinations are the heir (this finding) and the heir's claim payout (F20).

verifiedSound.lens: r2-frontend: irreversible address inputs and truncated display (AUDIT_SCOPE priority 7, no lens assigned)
verifiedSound.property: Horizon input bounds are enforced on-chain whatever the UI sends
verifiedSound.reasoning: extendHorizon (:611-631) requires a value above the current horizon, at least now + inactivityPeriod, and at most now + 36500 days. The prompt's NaN path is caught (:237-240). Tested: non-ISO forms and inputs with surrounding spaces give NaN, and `20460-01-01` gives NaN. A malformed date can only delay, never shorten, the heir's long-stop.

verifiedSound.lens: r2-frontend: irreversible address inputs and truncated display (AUDIT_SCOPE priority 7, no lens assigned)
verifiedSound.property: The full heir address is always recoverable on-chain
verifiedSound.reasoning: VaultCreated and BeneficiaryChanged index the full beneficiary (:192-208), and getVault returns it in full (:813). The defect is limited to the app's display and confirmation layer, so it can be fixed without redeploying the immutable contract.
